title: The Call of Abraham, part 1 of 5: the call, Canaan, Egypt, and the parting from Lot
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The age of the patriarchs in the ancient Near East, about four thousand years ago: people dressed in simple garments of wool or linen, undyed or dyed in earth colours, tents of black goat hair, tools of wood, stone and bronze, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

ABRAM.name: Abram
ABRAM.desc: Abram, a tall, strong, upright man who looks about sixty, with warm brown weathered skin, thick wavy dark hair heavily streaked with grey reaching his collar, a full grey-streaked beard, a strong straight nose and steady, thoughtful dark eyes, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved tunic of undyed cream wool with a brown leather belt and a deep russet-red wool mantle draped over his left shoulder, and simple leather sandals

SARAI.name: Sarai
SARAI.desc: Sarai, a strikingly beautiful, graceful woman who looks about forty-five, with warm brown skin, large dark eyes, high cheekbones and long wavy black hair with a few silver threads, her hair mostly covered by a long indigo-blue wool head shawl that falls over her shoulders, wearing an ankle-length long-sleeved dress of undyed cream wool with a woven belt of red and blue, and simple leather sandals

LOT.name: Lot
LOT.desc: Lot, Abram's nephew, a slim young man of about twenty-five with warm brown skin, curly dark-brown hair to his ears, a short sparse dark beard and quick, lively eyes, wearing a knee-length short-sleeved tunic of olive-green wool with a leather belt and a tan wool mantle rolled over one shoulder, and simple leather sandals

PHARAOH.name: Pharaoh
PHARAOH.desc: Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, a lean, proud man of about forty with reddish-brown skin, a clean-shaven face, high cheekbones and dark eyes lined with black kohl, wearing a blue-and-gold striped royal headcloth that covers all his hair and falls to his shoulders, with a small gold cobra at the brow, a broad collar of gold and blue beads, a long pleated robe of fine white linen with short sleeves and a gold belt, and gilded leather sandals

segs.text: Then the LORD said to Abram,
Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household, and go to the land I will show you.
I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.
I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you; and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.
So Abram departed, as the LORD had directed him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
And Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all the possessions and people they had acquired in Haran, and set out for the land of Canaan. When they came to the land of Canaan,
Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem. And at that time the Canaanites were in the land.
Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said,
I will give this land to your offspring.
So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.

From there Abram moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the LORD, and he called on the name of the LORD.
And Abram journeyed on toward the Negev.
Now there was a famine in the land. So Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe.
As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai,
Look, I know that you are a beautiful woman,
and when the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ Then they will kill me but will let you live.
Please say you are my sister, so that I will be treated well for your sake, and on account of you my life will be spared.
So when Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
When Pharaoh’s officials saw Sarai, they commended her to him, and she was taken into the palace of Pharaoh.
He treated Abram well on her account, and Abram acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels.
The LORD, however, afflicted Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Abram’s wife Sarai.
So Pharaoh summoned Abram and asked,
What have you done to me? Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?
Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and go!
Then Pharaoh gave his men orders concerning Abram, and they sent him away with his wife and all his possessions.
So Abram went up out of Egypt into the Negev—he and his wife and all his possessions—and Lot was with him.
And Abram had become extremely wealthy in livestock and silver and gold.
From the Negev he journeyed from place to place toward Bethel, until he came to the place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had formerly been pitched,
to the site where he had built the altar. And there Abram called on the name of the LORD.
Now Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents.
But the land was unable to support both of them while they stayed together, for they had so many possessions that they were unable to coexist.
And there was discord between the herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of Lot. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were also living in the land.
So Abram said to Lot,
Please let there be no contention between you and me, or between your herdsmen and my herdsmen. After all, we are kinsmen.
Is not the whole land before you? Now separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right; if you go to the right, I will go to the left.

And Lot looked out and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan, all the way to Zoar, was well watered like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt. (This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)
So Lot chose the whole plain of the Jordan for himself and set out toward the east. And Abram and Lot parted company.
Abram lived in the land of Canaan, but Lot settled in the cities of the plain and pitched his tent toward Sodom.
But the men of Sodom were wicked, sinning greatly against the LORD.
After Lot had departed, the LORD said to Abram,
Now lift up your eyes from the place where you are, and look to the north and south and east and west,
for all the land that you see, I will give to you and your offspring forever.
I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if one could count the dust of the earth, then your offspring could be counted.
Get up and walk around the land, through its length and breadth, for I will give it to you.
So Abram moved his tent and went to live near the Oaks of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar to the LORD.

stills.prompt: Character reference sheet of {PHARAOH}: a full-body front view standing and a head-and-shoulders portrait, side by side, calm expression, plain warm-grey background. One person only, shown twice. No tools, no weapons, empty hands. The plain warm-grey painted background fills the whole picture from edge to edge behind both views: no landscape, no sky, no ground plants, no buildings, no throne, no writing and no other people anywhere. The skin is the same reddish-brown in both views.

Then the LORD said to Abram: at night on a grassy rise outside a walled mud-brick town, {ABRAM}, stands alone and looks up, one hand half raised, as {GLORY}, breaks through the dark clouds and falls on him and on the grass around him. {ONE}. Wide view.

Close view of the face of {ABRAM}, at night, lifted toward a warm golden light that falls on him from above the frame, his eyes wide and natural, his lips parted, listening. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}.

I will make you into a great nation: {ABRAM}, kneels on one knee in the night grass with his head bowed and one hand on his chest, bathed in {GLORY}; far behind him the small dark shapes of a sleeping town. {ONE}. Medium view from the side.

In a lamplit room of a mud-brick house at night, {SARAI}, sits alone on a woven mat spinning wool with a wooden hand spindle, and {ABRAM}, has just come in and stands in the open doorway looking at her in silence, the night sky behind him. {TWO}. No children, no cradle. Medium view.

All the families of the earth will be blessed through you: seen from behind and a little above, {ABRAM}, kneels alone on a hilltop at first light, tiny before an immense land of plains, winding rivers and far blue mountains that stretches away to the horizon, while {GLORY}, spreads over the whole land. Exactly one person, seen from behind. Very wide view.

So Abram departed, and Lot went with him: at dawn in the courtyard of a mud-brick house, {ABRAM}, pulls tight the rope of a pack on a grey donkey, and {LOT}, walks up to him with a bundle on his shoulder and a staff in his hand, ready to travel. {TWOMEN}. Medium view.

Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran: {ABRAM}, walks toward us out of the open gate of a walled town of tan mud brick in the early morning, a wooden staff in his right hand, his face set and resolute. {ONE}. Medium view from the front.

Abram took his wife Sarai and his nephew Lot: three people walk side by side toward the viewer on a dusty road at the head of {CARAVAN}. From left to right they are: {LOT}, leading a grey donkey by its rope; {ABRAM}, in the middle with a staff; and {SARAI}, walking beside Abram. Exactly three people in front: two men and one woman. {NOCAMELS}. Medium-wide view.

All the possessions and people they had acquired in Haran: seen from a hillside, a long column leaves {HARANTOWN}: {SERVANTS}, walking beside donkeys loaded with rolled tents, baskets and water skins, driving flocks of sheep and goats along the road in a haze of golden dust. {NOCAMELS}. Wide high view.

When they came to the land of Canaan: seen from behind, a small group of travellers on foot with {CARAVAN}, come over a rocky pass and stop, looking out over {CANAAN}, spread out below them in clear morning light. In front, seen from behind: a man in a russet-red mantle with a staff, a woman in an indigo-blue head shawl and a young man in olive-green. {NOCAMELS}. Wide view over their shoulders.

Abram traveled through the land: {ABRAM}, walks from left to right along a stony path through {CANAAN}, leading a laden grey donkey by its rope, with sheep and goats following behind him. {ONE}. {NOCAMELS}. Wide view from the side.

As far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem: {OAK}, stands alone in a green valley between two hills, and beneath it, small beside the huge trunk, {ABRAM}, stands looking up into its branches with his staff in his hand. {ONE}. No buildings near the tree. Wide view.

At that time the Canaanites were in the land: in the foreground three {CANAANITES}, straighten up from hoeing a terraced field with wooden hoes and stare warily toward the viewer; behind them a path climbs to {CANAANTOWN}. Exactly three men in the foreground. Medium-wide view.

Then the LORD appeared to Abram: under the spreading branches of {OAK}, {ABRAM}, drops to his knees and raises one arm to shield his eyes as {GLORY}, streams down through the leaves in bright shafts. {ONE}. Medium-wide view.

I will give this land to your offspring: close view of {ABRAM}, kneeling, looking up with wonder, warm golden light on his face and green oak leaves behind him. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}.

So Abram built an altar there to the LORD: near the trunk of {OAK}, {ABRAM}, with his mantle laid aside over a branch, bends and sets a heavy rough field stone on top of {ALTAR}, which is half built. {NOFIRE}. {ONE}. Medium view.

From there Abram moved on to the hill country east of Bethel: seen from far off, a small column of people on foot with {CARAVAN}, moves along the crest of a long bare ridge in {CANAAN}, dark against a bright afternoon sky. {NOCAMELS}. Very wide view.

And pitched his tent: on a grassy hilltop, {ABRAM}, kneels driving a wooden tent peg into the ground with a wooden mallet, and {SARAI}, stands beside him holding a taut tent rope, with {TENT}, half raised behind them. {TWO}. Medium view.

{EMPTY}. With Bethel to the west and Ai to the east: in the middle of the picture, on a bare grassy ridge, stands one single {TENT}. {BETHELAI}. The low evening sun stands above the town on the left and long shadows fall toward the right. Very wide view.

There he built an altar to the LORD, and he called on the name of the LORD: at dusk on a hilltop, {ABRAM}, stands before {ALTAR}, with both hands lifted to shoulder height, palms up, and his face raised to the sky; a black goat-hair tent stands behind him. {NOFIRE}. {ONE}. Medium-wide view.

And Abram journeyed on toward the Negev: seen from behind, a small column of people on foot with {CARAVAN}, walks away from us down out of green hills into {NEGEV}. In front, seen from behind, a man in a russet-red mantle with a staff. {NOCAMELS}. Wide view from behind.

{EMPTY}. Now there was a famine in the land: a field of withered, stunted grain, brown and brittle, stands in cracked dry earth under a white burning sky, beside a stream bed that is nothing but dry stones; a dead leafless tree at one side. No animals. Wide low view.

The famine was severe: at the stone rim of a well in a dry valley, {ABRAM}, kneels and hauls up a leather bucket on a rope, tipping it to find it empty and dry, while a few thin sheep press around him with hanging heads. {ONE}. Medium view.

So Abram went down to Egypt: seen from behind and high up, a small column of people on foot with {CARAVAN}, crosses a tawny desert of sand and stone toward a distant strip of bright green land with a shining river on the horizon. No pyramids. {NOCAMELS}. Very wide high view.

As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai: beside a desert road at the edge of green fields and date palms, {ABRAM}, has stopped and turned to face {SARAI}, speaking to her in a low, urgent way with one hand raised; she stands listening, holding the lead rope of a grey donkey. {TWO}. Medium view.

I know that you are a beautiful woman: close view of the beautiful face of {SARAI}, in soft daylight, looking at someone out of frame with a questioning, troubled look, date palms blurred behind her. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.
Then they will kill me: close view of the face of {ABRAM}, in daylight, speaking earnestly with fear in his eyes, his brow furrowed. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

When the Egyptians see you: at a frontier post of whitewashed mud brick beside a canal lined with date palms, four {SOLDIERS}, stand in the road watching travellers approach, one of them shading his eyes with his hand. Exactly four soldiers. {NOHORSES}. Medium-wide view.

Please say you are my sister: {ABRAM}, holds both hands of {SARAI}, in his and leans toward her, pleading; she looks down at their joined hands, her face grave. They stand in the shade of a date palm. {TWO}. Medium close view.
{SARAI}, walks alone toward the viewer along a road between green fields, drawing her indigo-blue head shawl closer around her face with one hand, her eyes lowered. {ONE}. Medium view.

So when Abram entered Egypt: {ABRAM}, and {SARAI}, walk side by side toward the viewer down a crowded riverside market street of whitewashed mud-brick houses, among {EGYPTIANS}, who turn their heads to stare at her; baskets of grain, fish and onions stand at the sides. Medium-wide view.

The Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful: seen from behind in the foreground, a woman in an indigo-blue head shawl and a cream wool dress walks away from us through a market; facing us, a group of {EGYPTIANS}, have stopped beside a stall of clay jars and stare at her, one man whispering to another. Medium view.

When Pharaoh's officials saw Sarai: in the foreground {SARAI}, lifts a clay water jar at a stone well in a sunlit square; behind her, on the shaded steps of a whitewashed building, stand three of {OFFICIALS}, and one of them points her out to the others. Exactly four people: one woman and three officials. Medium-wide view.

They commended her to him: in {HALL}, {PHARAOH}, sits on a wooden throne with gilded legs on a low platform, leaning forward with interest, while before him two of {OFFICIALS}, bow low, one of them gesturing with an open hand as he speaks. Exactly three people. Medium-wide view.

And she was taken into the palace of Pharaoh: {SARAI}, is led away from us between two of {OFFICIALS}, toward the tall open gateway of {PALACE}; she looks back over her shoulder toward the viewer with a frightened face. Exactly three people. Medium-wide view.

He treated Abram well on her account; Abram acquired sheep and cattle: at a camp of black tents beside green fields, a clean-shaven Egyptian steward in a long white linen robe waves forward a flock of sheep and a herd of brown long-horned cattle toward {ABRAM}, who stands with his arms at his sides and takes no joy in it, his face heavy. Exactly two men. Medium-wide view.

Male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels: a line of tall tan one-humped camels and grey donkeys is led by their ropes from left to right past black tents by {SERVANTS}, with date palms and a broad river behind. Wide view from the side.

At night, {ABRAM}, sits alone on the ground outside a black goat-hair tent among sleeping sheep and kneeling camels, gazing at the far lamplit walls of a great whitewashed palace across dark fields. {ONE}. Wide view.

The LORD afflicted Pharaoh with severe plagues: in a lamplit chamber of the palace at night, {PHARAOH}, lies sick on a couch with carved wooden legs, pale and sweating, one hand pressed to his brow, while a servant in a white linen kilt and tunic kneels beside him holding out a bowl of water. Exactly two people. No wounds, no blood. Medium view.

And his household: along {HALL}, at night, many {EGYPTIANS}, lie sick on reed mats on the floor or sit slumped against the columns holding their heads, while one old man in a white linen robe goes among them with a clay cup. No wounds, no blood, no one dead. Wide view down the hall.

Because of Abram's wife Sarai: in a small room of the palace with a high window, {SARAI}, sits alone and well on a cushioned bench with her hands clasped in her lap, looking up at a shaft of daylight that falls through the window onto her. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium view.

So Pharaoh summoned Abram: in {HALL}, {PHARAOH}, pale and angry, has risen from his throne and points at {ABRAM}, who stands before him with his head lowered and his hands empty. Two {SOLDIERS}, stand in the background beside the door. Pharaoh is on the left and Abram on the right. Medium-wide view.
What have you done to me?: close view of the face of {PHARAOH}, pale and drawn from sickness, his kohl-lined eyes wide with anger, speaking. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

Now then, here is your wife: in {HALL}, three people stand. From left to right they are: {PHARAOH}, gesturing with a stiff open hand; {SARAI}, in the middle, walking away from Pharaoh toward Abram; and {ABRAM}, on the right, holding out one hand to her. Exactly three people: two men and one woman. Medium-wide view.

Why did you say, She is my sister?: close view of {ABRAM}, and {SARAI}, standing side by side in the pillared hall; he looks down in shame and she looks at him steadily. Head and shoulders of both. {TWO}.

Take her and go!: {PHARAOH}, stands in front of his throne and flings out his right arm, pointing toward the bright open doorway at the far end of the pillared hall. {ONE}. Medium view from a low angle.

Then Pharaoh gave his men orders concerning Abram: at the top of the palace steps, {PHARAOH}, speaks sternly to a captain of {SOLDIERS}, who bows his head with his fist on his chest; three more soldiers stand behind the captain. Medium-wide view.

And they sent him away with his wife: {ABRAM}, and {SARAI}, walk side by side toward the viewer along a road beside a canal, and close behind them walk four {SOLDIERS}, escorting them out. Exactly two travellers in front and four soldiers behind. {NOHORSES}. Medium-wide view.

And all his possessions: seen from high up, {RICHCARAVAN}, with many people on foot, streams away from a whitewashed palace and green fields along a road toward the open tawny desert, while a line of {SOLDIERS}, stands along the road watching it go. No pyramids. {NOHORSES}. Very wide high view.

So Abram went up out of Egypt into the Negev, he and his wife, and Lot was with him: three people climb a stony desert road toward the viewer at the head of {RICHCARAVAN}. From left to right they are: {SARAI}; {ABRAM}, in the middle with a staff; and {LOT}, leading a tan one-humped camel by its rope. Exactly three people in front: two men and one woman. Dry pale hills behind. Medium-wide view.

Abram had become extremely wealthy in livestock and silver and gold: in a camp of black tents, {ABRAM}, stands beside an open wooden chest filled with silver rings, silver bars and gold bracelets that gleam in the sun, and behind him great herds of cattle, sheep and camels cover the dry hillside. There are no coins. {ONE}. Medium-wide view.

From the Negev he journeyed from place to place toward Bethel: {ABRAM}, walks from left to right up a grassy ridge in {CANAAN}, ahead of a long line of camels, donkeys and sheep, looking ahead and shading his eyes as if he knows the place. {ONE}. Wide view from the side.

To the site where he had built the altar: on a bare grassy hilltop, {ABRAM}, stands with one hand laid on the top of {ALTAR}, which is old and weathered now, with dry grass grown up around its foot and lichen on its stones. {NOFIRE}. {ONE}. Medium view.

And there Abram called on the name of the LORD: {ABRAM}, kneels on both knees before {ALTAR}, on a hilltop at sunrise, his hands lifted and open and his face raised to the bright sky. {NOFIRE}. {ONE}. Medium-wide view from the side.

Now Lot also had flocks and herds and tents: {LOT}, walks among his own sheep, goats and brown cattle with a herdsman's staff, counting them with a pointing finger, and behind him stands a row of black goat-hair tents. {ONE}. Medium-wide view.

The land was unable to support both of them: seen from above, a narrow valley in the hills is packed from side to side with sheep, goats, cattle and camels, the grass eaten down to bare dusty earth, with two separate clusters of black tents crowded close on either side and a few {HERDSMEN}, among the animals. Wide high view.

And there was discord between the herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of Lot: at a stone well trampled to mud, two groups of {HERDSMEN}, three on the left and three on the right, shout at each other and shove, two of them gripping each other's tunics, their thirsty sheep and cattle crowding around them. Exactly six men. No blood, no weapons but wooden staffs. Medium-wide view.

At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were also living in the land: from the top of the wall of {CANAANTOWN}, seen from behind, three {CANAANITES}, with bronze-headed spears look down into a valley crowded with a stranger's herds and black tents. Exactly three men, seen from behind. Wide view over their shoulders.

So Abram said to Lot, Please let there be no contention between you and me: on a hillside above the camps, {ABRAM}, lays his hand on the shoulder of {LOT}, and speaks to him gently; Lot stands with folded arms, listening. Abram is on the left and Lot on the right. {TWOMEN}. Medium view.
After all, we are kinsmen: close view of the face of {ABRAM}, in daylight, speaking kindly and earnestly with a slight, tired smile. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.

Is not the whole land before you?: on a high rocky hilltop, {ABRAM}, sweeps his right arm wide across a vast view of hills and a far green valley, and {LOT}, beside him follows the gesture with his eyes. {TWOMEN}. Wide view from the side and a little behind them.

If you go to the left, I will go to the right: {ABRAM}, stands facing the viewer on a hilltop with both arms held out, one open hand to the left and one open hand to the right, offering the choice, the sky wide behind him. {ONE}. Medium view from the front.
And Lot looked out: close view of {LOT}, on a hilltop, shading his eyes with one hand and gazing into the distance with eager, widening eyes, wind in his hair. Head and shoulders only. {ONE}.
{EMPTY}. The whole plain of the Jordan was well watered: {JORDAN}, stretching away between two walls of dry mountains to a far haze. Very wide high view.

{EMPTY}. Like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt: a very close, low view of clear water running along a narrow earth channel between heavy-headed green barley, date palms hung with fruit and flowering bushes, sunlight sparkling on the water. No buildings.

This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah: seen from far off and high up in calm morning light, two cities stand whole and prosperous on the green valley floor, each of them {SODOM}. Both cities are intact, with no fire, no smoke and no ruins anywhere. No people near. Very wide high view.

So Lot chose the whole plain of the Jordan for himself: on the hilltop, {LOT}, on the left, points down with his whole arm toward the green valley far below, his face eager, while {ABRAM}, on the right, stands quietly watching him. {TWOMEN}. Medium-wide view.

And Abram and Lot parted company: {ABRAM}, and {LOT}, clasp each other's forearms in farewell on a stony path in early morning light, looking each other in the face; behind Lot his loaded donkeys wait. {TWOMEN}. Medium view.

And set out toward the east: seen from the side, {LOT}, walks from left to right down a steep stony track with a staff, leading a laden camel, with his flocks, herds and herdsmen following, toward the rising sun low on the right and a green valley far below. Wide view.

Seen from behind, a tall man with grey-streaked dark hair in an ankle-length cream wool tunic and a deep russet-red mantle stands alone on a hilltop with a staff, watching a small caravan far below wind away down toward a green valley in the morning sun. Exactly one man in the foreground, seen from behind. Wide view from behind.

card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 12:1–13:18, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 12:1-20 and 13:1-18 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, G the voice of God (as in earlier units), A Abram (12:11-13, 13:8-9), F Pharaoh (12:18-19). Voices A and F are first choices nobody has heard; change them freely at assembly.
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. REF = character reference sheet (not used in the film, no clip). Still 'verses' are chapter:verse.

Faces: ABRAM, SARAI and LOT use the sheets and description text of s01e03b word for word (Abram is 75 at 12:4 and is painted as a vigorous man who looks about sixty; Sarai is called beautiful at 12:11 and 12:14). New in this unit: refs/REF-PHARAOH.jpg (key PHARAOH), the unnamed Pharaoh of Genesis 12 only; he is not the Pharaoh of Joseph or of the Exodus and must not be reused for them.
God is light only (GLORY). 'The LORD appeared to Abram' (12:7): the text does not say in what form; shown as light through the oak, never a figure. The speech of 13:14-17 is light on a hilltop.

Altars (12:7, 12:8, 13:4, 13:18): unhewn field stones (I). The text names no sacrifice at any of them, so no fire, smoke or animal is shown on them; 'called on the name of the LORD' is Abram with lifted hands (I).

The Oak of Moreh and the Oaks of Mamre follow the BSB wording (oak; the Hebrew can also be read terebinth). 12:8 'Bethel to the west and Ai to the east' is pictured as a tent between two far hill towns with the evening sun over the left-hand one (H3, I). The Canaanites and Perizzites (12:6, 13:7) are townsmen and watchers on a wall (costume I).
No camels are shown before 12:16, where the text first names them; from then on Abram's and Lot's caravans include them (T). Silver and gold (13:2) are rings, bars and bracelets, not coins (I).

Egypt (12:10-20): the Pharaoh is unnamed and the date is disputed, so no pyramids, sphinx, obelisks or writing are shown and no dynasty is implied; dress is generic (white linen, striped royal headcloth, I). Sarai is 'taken into the palace' (12:15) and Pharaoh says 'I took her as my wife' (12:19): she is shown only being led through the gate (O3) and later sitting alone and well (Q3, I); nothing else is pictured and what happened in the palace is not resolved. The 'severe plagues' (12:17) are of no stated kind: Pharaoh and his household are shown sick, with no sores, wounds or deaths (I). How Pharaoh learned the cause is not told and not pictured. Sarai speaks no word in the text and none is given her; M2 (she walks on with lowered eyes) is D. Abram gives no answer to Pharaoh in the text and none is shown.
12:12: what Abram fears is not pictured as happening; L2 shows only Egyptian soldiers at a frontier post (I).

13:10-13: the plain of the Jordan and its cities are shown whole, green and prosperous, in the text's own order ('before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah'): no fire or ruin is shown or foreshadowed. Where the cities stood is disputed and is not resolved (a green valley floor; no map). 13:13 says only that the men of Sodom were wicked: AF1 (a traveller robbed in a street) and AF2 (the torchlit city under a dark sky) are D and do not say what the sin was.

13:14: the four views (AG3 north with a far snow mountain, AG4 south to desert, AH1 east to the Jordan valley, AH2 west to the sea) are I from the geography of the hill country near Bethel. 13:9 left and right are not turned into compass directions.
AD4 (Abram from behind watching Lot's caravan go) and P3 (Abram alone at night looking at the palace) are D.
Narration is not generated in this unit; shots are laid at assembly.
